style: a punchy history storyteller with dry humour, respectful, building to a powerful ending

lines.text: He was born enslaved. He ended up running an entire island.
Toussaint Louverture, born around 1743, in the French colony of Saint-Domingue.
In 1791, the enslaved rose up. He joined them, and became their sharpest general.
By 1801, he governed the whole island, with his own constitution.
Then France invited him to a meeting. It was a trap.
On the ship, he reportedly said: you have only cut down the trunk of the tree of liberty.
He died in a French prison in 1803. A few months later, Haiti was free.
lines.direct: quiet, then proud and warm on the last words
